title: Autoregressive drift gate with windowed fallback for throughput/latency sanity
author: Priya Anand
release_notes: Adds an autoregressive drift detector gate that isolates and mitigates short-lived throughput/latency regressions with a windowed fallback policy; exposes config knobs for forecast horizon, sensitivity, and cooldown; integrates with canary evaluator and Console alerts; no API-breaking changes.
description:
Context: We observed a class of short-lived throughput regressions that map to traffic seasonality and subtle scheduler-induced jitter. Existing canary detectors flagged absolute deltas but were noisy during diurnal shifts, causing unnecessary rollbacks. This PR implements an autoregressive residual-based drift gate (AR-Drift) plus a conservative windowed fallback that temporarily routes traffic to a conservative model/pool when a forecasted deviation exceeds configurable bounds.

Summary of changes and motivation:
- Implemented an AR-based time-series residual detector that models short-term seasonality and produces a probabilistic drift score instead of a single-delta metric. The detector uses an online AR(1)/AR(2) estimator with exponentially-weighted windowing to avoid heavy state while remaining adaptive to traffic shape changes.
- Added a windowed fallback policy: when the drift score crosses the sensitivity threshold for N consecutive evaluation windows, the controller triggers a soft fallback. The soft fallback pins routing to a lower-throughput-but-stable variant, increases replica headroom, enables KV-cache warming, and emits a high-severity telemetry marker. The fallback has an exponential backoff cooldown to prevent oscillation.
- Integrations: AR-Drift is plumbed into the canary evaluator pipeline (perf-canary) as a supplemental signal, to the Console for runtime dashboarding and a new alert rule, and to the rollout controller so the gate can be used as a rollout guard with canary weight damping.
- Safety and ops: feature is off by default; toggles exist at route and tenant level; a kill-switch metric and manual override are available in the Console. There is a conservative default profile tuned for 99th-percentile sensitivity so we don't cause unnecessary user-visible regressions.

Commits (high level):
- c1be9d2: initial AR-Drift prototype and core estimator, detector interface, unit tests.
- a7f3f1b: integrate detector with perf-canary evaluator, add synthetic seasonality probe and harness tests.
- e2d4c6a: fallback policy, rollout-controller integration, docs, Console wiring, lint/tests fixes.

Files/areas touched (high level):
- pkg/canary/ardrift_gate.go (detector + gate logic)
- pkg/canary/ardrift_gate_test.go (unit tests for estimator, thresholds, hysteresis)
- perf-canary/configs/seasonality_probe.yaml (synthetic probe config used in integration tests)
- controllers/rollout/gates.go (hook to consult AR-Drift gate before step-up)
- infra/k8s/rollout-gates.yaml (operator config and RBAC)
- docs/canaries/ardrift.md (design doc, ops runbook, toggles)
- console/dashboards/canary-ardrift.json (dashboard panel and alert rule)

Review thread summary:
- Jonah Kim: requested a clear explanation for hysteresis/cooldown math and suggested adding a synthetic probe to validate against diurnal patterns. Also asked for a telemetry event to include model variant and replica snapshot for postmortems.
- Priya: added a synthetic seasonality probe under perf-canary and extended the telemetry event payload; updated tests to include multiple day-like windows.
- Marta Rivers: raised a concern around the default sensitivity being too aggressive for low-traffic routes; requested route-level overrides and a tenant opt-out.
- Priya: exposed route/tenant toggles and added an opt-out flag; adjusted the default profile to be more conservative for <10r/s routes.
- Ethan Cole: ran a canary in the staging perf-lab and reported no regressions; asked for an e2e job to be added to pipeline.
- Priya: added an integration stage to the perf-canary pipeline and re-ran CI.

CI and verification:
- Initial CI: failed lint on console JSON (missing comma) and one flaky test in ardrift_gate_test.go.
- Fixes: corrected linting issues and hardened test timing; re-ran CI.
- Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration perf-canary, e2e synthetic canary run).

Testing notes:
- Unit coverage added for estimator state transitions, false-positive suppression, and cooldown backoff.
- Integration test simulates diurnal traffic ramp and verifies detector maintains low false-positive rate and triggers fallback within expected windows when injected anomalies present.
- Staging run: deployed to a dedicated perf-lab cluster, ran synthetic probe over 24h compressed window; fallback triggered once under injected anomaly and automatic recovery worked as expected.

Operational knobs and configs (defaults):
- forecast_horizon: "2 windows"
- sensitivity_q: "0.995"
- consecutive_windows_for_trigger: "3"
- fallback_duration_initial: "5m"
- cooldown_backoff: "x2"
- enable_route_override: "true"

Metrics and logs added:
- canary.ardrift.score (gauge)
- canary.ardrift.trigger_count (counter)
- canary.ardrift.fallback_active (gauge)
- telemetry events: canary/ardrift/fallback with route/model/replica snapshot.

Docs and runbook: docs/canaries/ardrift.md includes background, config guide, expected signal patterns, troubleshooting steps, example CLI toggles, and rollback procedures.

Ops impact and risk: The feature is opt-in per-route and under a feature flag tenant-wide. Default profile errs on the side of silence for low-traffic routes. Primary risk is unintended traffic pinning if sensitivity is misconfigured; mitigations include a short default fallback, exponential cooldown, and visible Console alerting.

Merge notes: after sign-off from reviewers and a green CI run with the new perf-canary e2e stage, PR was squashed and merged by Marta Rivers.

Post-merge follow-ups:
- ENG-8701: add a canary-canary job to exercise the gate under more traffic shapes.
- ENG-8599: collect a week's worth of ardrift.score metrics and run offline analysis to tune defaults.
